What is WellSaid?

Enterprise text-to-speech platform built on voices licensed from paid, consenting voice actors, marketed on ethical sourcing and consistency for corporate training and product narration rather than on cloning arbitrary voices.

Best for

Consistent corporate narration with ethically licensed voices and controlled pronunciation.

Main features

  • Voice Avatars built from contracted voice actors who are compensated for usage
  • studio-quality corporate narration voices
  • pronunciation library and custom lexicons for brand and technical terms
  • scriptwriting and editing workspace
  • team collaboration with shared pronunciation libraries
  • SSML-style controls
  • Caption and Studio features
  • SOC 2 Type II compliance
  • API.

Practical use cases

  • Narrating a large e-learning catalogue with consistent voice and pronunciation
  • producing training audio that must be updated frequently
  • corporate explainer and product videos
  • IVR and telephony prompts
  • accessibility narration.

Who is it for?

  • Corporate L&D teams, instructional designers, e-learning agencies, product marketing, and organisations with ethical-sourcing requirements.

Pricing, free access & limits

Per-seat subscription with usage tiers; enterprise licensing

Plans described in the source

Maker around $44/mo ($24-29/mo billed annually) for 1 seat and a limited monthly usage allowance. Creative around $89/mo ($44-79 annually) with more voices and downloads. Team/Business around $179+/mo with multiple seats and shared libraries. Enterprise custom, annual, with unlimited usage, custom voice avatars, SSO and dedicated support. Verify - WellSaid has repositioned tiers since its enterprise pivot.

Free plan

No permanent free plan.

Free trial

Yes - free trial (typically 7 days) with limited downloads.

Usage limits to consider

Metered by downloads/characters per month by tier. Custom Voice Avatar creation is enterprise-only and carries a separate fee plus voice-actor contracting. Seat counts are tier-limited.

Strengths & tradeoffs

These points summarize the supplied research, rather than hands-on test results.

Strengths noted in the source

  • The ethical sourcing model - real voice actors who are contracted and paid for usage - is a defensible procurement position that matters to some organisations and unions
  • pronunciation libraries shared across a team solve a real problem in technical and pharmaceutical training
  • voice consistency across a large catalogue is excellent
  • strong e-learning tool integrations.

Limitations to consider

  • English-centric to the point of being unusable for multilingual organisations - this is the single biggest limitation versus ElevenLabs or Synthesia
  • expensive per seat for the output volume
  • no arbitrary voice cloning (by design, but a limitation if you need it)
  • smaller voice library
  • less natural on expressive or conversational delivery than ElevenLabs.

Platforms, languages & integrations

Platforms

  • Web (WellSaid Studio)
  • API

Languages

  • Primarily English with multiple accents (US, UK, AU); limited non-English coverage - notably weak for Arabic

API access

Yes - WellSaid API for programmatic generation on higher tiers

Integrations and exports

  • Articulate Storyline and Rise, Adobe Captivate, Camtasia, Zapier, LMS platforms via audio export

Evaluation notes

Rule this out immediately if you need Arabic or broad multilingual output. Its honest niche is English-language corporate e-learning where ethical sourcing is a procurement requirement.
